s0271.literal: At the beginning of Han, those who transmitted the Changes included Tian He; He taught Ding Kuan; Kuan taught Tian Wangsun; Wangsun taught Shi Chou of Pei, Meng Xi of Donghai, and Liangqiu He of Langye.
s0271.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, those who transmitted the Changes included Tian He; He taught Ding Kuan; Kuan taught Tian Wangsun; Wangsun taught Shi Chou of Pei, Meng Xi of Donghai, and Liangqiu He of Langye.

s0272.literal: Hence there were the schools of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu.
s0272.idiomatic: Hence there were the schools of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu.

s0273.literal: There was also Jing Fang of Dongjun, who claimed to have received the Changes from Jiao Yanshou of Liang, forming a separate Jing school.
s0273.idiomatic: There was also Jing Fang of Dongjun, who claimed to have received the Changes from Jiao Yanshou of Liang, forming a separate Jing school.

s0274.literal: It was once established, then later abolished.
s0274.idiomatic: It was once established, then later abolished.

s0275.literal: In Later Han the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools—four in all—were simultaneously established, and those who transmitted them were very numerous.
s0275.idiomatic: In Later Han the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools—four in all—were simultaneously established, and those who transmitted them were very numerous.

s0276.literal: At the beginning of Han there was also Fei Zhi of Donglai, who transmitted the Changes; his text was entirely in ancient characters, called the Old Text Changes.
s0276.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han there was also Fei Zhi of Donglai, who transmitted the Changes; his text was entirely in ancient characters, called the Old Text Changes.

s0277.literal: He taught Wang Huang of Langye; Huang taught Gao Xiang of Pei; Xiang taught his son Kang and Jiang Yong of Lanling.
s0277.idiomatic: He taught Wang Huang of Langye; Huang taught Gao Xiang of Pei; Xiang taught his son Kang and Jiang Yong of Lanling.

s0278.literal: Hence there was the Fei school, circulating among the people but not established at court.
s0278.idiomatic: Hence there was the Fei school, circulating among the people but not established at court.

s0279.literal: In Later Han Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong both transmitted the Fei school.
s0279.idiomatic: In Later Han Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong both transmitted the Fei school.

s0280.literal: Ma Rong also transmitted it and taught Zheng Xuan.

s0282.literal: In Wei, Wang Su and Wang Bi both annotated it.
s0282.idiomatic: In Wei, Wang Su and Wang Bi both annotated it.

s0283.literal: From this time the Fei school flourished greatly and the Gao school declined.
s0283.idiomatic: From this time the Fei school flourished greatly and the Gao school declined.

s0284.literal: The Liangqiu, Shi, and Gao schools perished in Western Jin.

s0285.literal: The Meng and Jing schools had books but no teachers.
s0285.idiomatic: The Meng and Jing schools had books but no teachers.

s0287.literal: In Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.
s0287.idiomatic: In Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.

s0288.literal: By Sui, Wang's commentary prevailed and Zheng's learning gradually faded; today it is nearly extinct.
s0288.idiomatic: By Sui, Wang's commentary prevailed and Zheng's learning gradually faded; today it is nearly extinct.

s0289.literal: The Hidden Storehouse was already lost at the beginning of Han; examining Jin's Inner Canon, it was present, but it recorded only divination and did not resemble the purport of the sages.
